correctness.rationale: The mixed discrete difference is exactly the q-fold iterated integral of theta^(q), normalized by the product of the q dyadic increments. Uniform continuity controls the derivative-norm limit and quantitative modulus error. Boolean degree <=q-1 annihilates this interaction; the converse follows by substituting binary expansions into real polynomials. One-sign derivative gives a strict uniform approximation lower bound by the triangle inequality; the exponential face optimum is attained by an alternating-sign correction. Exact rational and numerical reproducibility tests, 2644 checks, corroborate identities but do not replace proofs.

value.rationale: The paper motivating the question charges Boolean-angle degree to quantum quadrature oracle cost at one grid resolution while its quadrature analysis requires refining n. The new result completely characterizes smooth integrands that retain any fixed low interaction degree at every refinement, detects curvature through a sharp normalized bit coefficient, and proves a strictly positive approximation-error floor for curved angles independent of grid refinement. This directly addresses when low-degree encoding remains viable across resolutions, not an arbitrary finite table computation; circuit-model limits are explicit.
